sources.title: Efficient Quantum State Preparation with Walsh Series
sources.anchor: arXiv v3, 9 November 2023; checked 29 September 2026: Theorem 1, Corollary 1, Table I and Appendix B (B14–B19, B28).
sources.scope: Walsh Series Loader: epsilon is state infidelity. Smooth fixed-function single-attempt depth O(epsilon^-1/2), size O(n+epsilon^-1/2), success Theta(epsilon); expected depth O(epsilon^-3/2), expected size O((n+epsilon^-1/2)/epsilon). Constants retain function/derivative/nonzero-mass assumptions. Sparse variants require supplied coefficients and Hamming-weight bounds. Amplification also charges reflections and inverses.

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Circuits for Non-Unitary and Unitary Diagonal Operators with Space-Time-Accuracy trade-offs
sources.authors: Julien Zylberman; Ugo Nzongani; Andrea Simonetto; Fabrice Debbasch
sources.anchor: arXiv v4, 21 January 2025; checked 29 September 2026: II.1, III.1–III.2, IV.1 Eqs. (15)–(16), V.1 Eqs. (19)–(21), VI A, VIII.1 and Tables I–II. Figure 4 signal-sector and III.2/VIII.1 accounting ambiguities remain explicit source obligations.
sources.scope: Parallel scheduling trades ancillas for depth, not automatically total size. Table I uses spectral-norm error; Eq. (18) bounds normalized-block error delta, corresponding to total-scale times delta in the unscaled-operator convention. Exact-block success in source notation is ||D psi||^2/(alpha^2 dmax^2); alpha>1 controls the transformed-angle derivative in smooth approximation. No local source theorem or resolution of source ambiguities is claimed.
